title: Random forest prioritizes dual-stage antimalarial compounds
summary: A random forest trained on parasite activity data screened commercial compounds; 100 predicted actives and 20 predicted inactives were tested. The primary manuscript reports 18 dose-response-validated compounds with liver- and blood-stage activity among 26 liver-stage hits. The selected sets are not population samples, and assays used P. berghei liver-stage and P. falciparum blood-stage parasites.
organization: Rutgers University–New Jersey Medical School; Duke University

evidence.tested: Primary indexed Methods/Results report 18 dual-stage validated compounds and screening denominators.
evidence.unknown: Chemical prior art, complete supplemental details and clinical translation remain open; do not present 18/26 as general hit rate.
evidence.ai_role: Classifier prioritizes compounds from >1.5 million virtual candidates; human structural-diversity selection and assays follow.

source_review.scope: PMC-indexed primary manuscript text; publisher primary metadata/index. Material checked for the specific claims stated in the record.
